text:
Kara (Customer): Hey team — since ~10:12 UTC we're seeing p95 jump from ~120ms to ~1.8-2s for EU clients. Client reports requests are being served from us-east-1 even though they advertise eu-west-1. trace-id=abc123. Any idea why regional routing is falling back like this?

Maya (Support): Sorry about that — can you paste the raw request (curl or headers) and the trace-id? Also which API key/tenant? I'll poke the routing probes.

Kara (Customer): trace-id=abc123. Request used tenant 'acme-inc'. Example repro:
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-live-REDACTED" -H "X-Client-Region: eu-west-1" https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
```
Response headers included: `x-redwood-edge: us-east-1`, `x-request-id: abc123`. Timings: connect 48ms, tls 80ms, first_byte 350ms, total 1900ms.

Samir (SRE): Looking at our tracewalk for abc123 — initial anycast landed in apac-pop-2 then got forwarded to us-east-edge-03 before it finally hit eu-west-1-origin. That extra leg explains the ~1.6s delta. Pasting abbreviated trace:
```
tracewalk abc123
[10:12:14] client -> apac-pop-2 (anycast)
[10:12:14] apac-pop-2 -> us-east-edge-03 (unexpected leap)
[10:12:15] us-east-edge-03 -> eu-west-1-origin
[10:12:15] origin -> eu-west-1-backend
```
Looks like apac-pop-2 decided to proxy to a us-east edge rather than directly to eu-west.

Alex (Infra): We rolled a canary of the new edge-proxy to apac-pop-2 at 10:09 UTC. There's a config oversight in the fallback_policy that prefers a cheaper long-haul hop for some /24s — that would cause the APAC pop to choose the us-east transit instead of the eu-west direct path. I'm rolling the canary back now (started rollback 10:25 UTC).

tracebot: deploy-bot: Canary rollback initiated for service=edge-proxy on apac-pop-2 by Alex at 2026-06-12T10:25:12Z. Incident INC-2026-4321 opened.

Maya (Support): Workaround for customers in the short term: set header `X-Prefer-Region: eu-west-1` or use the regional endpoint `https://eu-west.api.redwood.example/v1/generate`. That forces region-affinity and avoids the unexpected proxy path until rollback finishes.

Kara (Customer): Applied `X-Prefer-Region`, retested — p95 back to ~130ms. Thanks. :relieved: Can you confirm whether this will affect billing or require any quota/billing reconciliation?

Samir (SRE): We'll quantify request volume affected. Preliminary numbers: ~0.02% of global requests hit the misroute during the canary window. Latency impact is localized but SLA hit potential exists for those customers. Cost delta negligible but we will include a billing note in the postmortem if needed.

Maya (Support): Copying routing/infra for a full RCA and follow-up with the customer. Escalating to @Alex for postmortem and mitigation plan.

Alex (Infra): Will produce RCA and add action items: tighten fallback_policy tests, add synthetic probes for anycast->region mismatches, and gate canary by path-level routing checks.

Kara (Customer): Thanks everyone — please keep me posted on RCA and timeline for a permanent fix.
